Mercy in our faith

Awareness sessions

We hold sessions in neighborhoods, colleges, community halls and schools, with one message every time: animals feel pain, animals feel fear, and animals deserve the mercy we hope for ourselves.

Online sessions, interviews & Boot Camp

Our online sessions bring veterinary guidance and animal-rights awareness to anyone with a phone. On 13 September 2026, Dr. Naveed Iqbal, DVM, was our guest speaker on Animal Welfare & Animal Rights Awareness over Google Meet. On 9 September 2026, our founder joined host and journalist Meer Emran Baloch for an online podcast interview on animal welfare and advocacy. In Khuzdar, at a Boot Camp, we also distributed awareness posters among students of different institutions.

Animal first aid

Found an injured or sick animal? These quick steps can help before a vet or our team arrives. Tap a card to open it.

Safety first. A frightened animal can bite or scratch. Keep your face away, move slowly, and never put yourself at risk.
🚗Hit by a vehicle / injured
  1. Stay calm and check the road is safe for you first.
  2. Approach slowly from the side. Hurt animals may bite out of fear.
  3. Cover the head gently with a cloth or jacket to calm it.
  4. Slide it onto a blanket, towel or board, keeping the body flat and the neck straight.
  5. Keep it warm and take it to a vet straight away.

Do not: lift by the legs or give food and water if it is drowsy or unconscious.

🩸Bleeding wound
  1. Press a clean cloth firmly on the wound for 5 to 10 minutes.
  2. If the cloth soaks through, add more on top. Do not remove the first one.
  3. Bandage lightly, not tight, and go to a vet.

Do not: put powders, toothpaste, oil or home remedies in a wound.

❄️Cold and winter
  1. Dry the animal with a towel or cloth.
  2. Wrap it in a blanket and place it in a sheltered, warm spot.
  3. Offer lukewarm water. Give food once it is alert.
  4. Put out a straw-lined box or sack shelter for strays.

Do not: use boiling water, or place it right against a heater.

☀️Heat stroke (summer)

Signs: heavy panting, drooling, weakness, collapse.

  1. Move to shade right away.
  2. Wet the paws, belly and ears with cool tap water.
  3. Offer small sips of water.
  4. Go to a vet, even if it seems to recover.

Do not: use ice-cold water, which can cause shock.

☠️Suspected poisoning

Signs: drooling, vomiting, shaking, stumbling, seizures.

  1. Move it away from the source.
  2. Take a photo of the substance or its packaging if you can.
  3. Keep it warm and calm and get to a vet immediately.

Do not: force vomiting, or give milk, salt water or any medicine unless a vet says so.

🐕Bites and scratches (for people)
  1. Wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes.
  2. Go to a hospital or clinic the same day to ask about rabies vaccination.
  3. Tell us or local authorities so the animal can be safely watched.

Do not: chase, hit or corner the animal, or ignore a bite because it looks small.

🐾Found puppies or kittens
  1. Watch from a distance for a few hours. The mother is often just away.
  2. If she does not return, or they are cold or hurt, wrap them in a soft cloth and keep them warm.
  3. Message us for guidance and feeding help.

Do not: give cow milk or human food to very young babies.

💊Never give human medicine

Common medicines such as paracetamol and ibuprofen can seriously harm animals. Also avoid chocolate, onions, grapes and sweets.

Always ask a vet before giving any medicine.

Not sure what to do? Send us a photo and the location.

A word from the founder

I am not a scholar. I am not a veterinarian. I am simply a man who, one ordinary night, asked himself an extraordinary question, and an animal answered it for me.

This is not about me. It is about a dog shivering outside a hotel, a WhatsApp group that grew into a family, and more than four hundred people who decided that mercy should not be optional.

Our motto“Be the HUMAN an ANIMAL needs when everyone FAILS them”

Jahangeer Ejaz Zehri

Founder, The Animal Welfare Network

The dog who disturbed no one

In loving memory · A story from Hyderabad, Sindh

For four years, Rabeet Naeem Khanzada fed and watched over a gentle dog near her home, the calmest she had ever known. When she returned from a trip to Karachi in September, her dog had been poisoned.

She never disturbed anyone. She never harmed anyone. She lived quietly, and she was loved.“Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed, to Him we shall return.” Qur’an 2:156

Rabeet has never been a silent witness. She raises her voice for animal rights, and for the dog who can no longer speak. A true animal activist. A true human being.

Our agenda: helping animals

Everything we do returns to one simple agenda. This is what we ask of ourselves, and what we invite you to join.

  1. Feed and shelter strays in your own street, every single day.
  2. Rescue and treat injured or sick animals without delay.
  3. Speak up and report cruelty whenever you witness it.
  4. Host or attend awareness sessions in your community.
  5. Teach children early that mercy to animals is mercy to all.
  6. Treat this as an act of faith, not a favor to be praised for.

Looking ahead

We hope for more feeding points, more rescue capacity, more awareness sessions, and more young people who choose compassion as a habit, not an event.

We dream of a day when no dog shivers unnoticed outside a building full of people, and every one of those people has somewhere to turn.
